image.alt: A Calathea Golden Mosaic with glossy leaves splashed in gold and dark green, in a white pot

light.label: Medium to bright indirect light
light.note: Not suited to low light; the gold fades

landscape_use.note: Frost-free, humid zones only; needs shade

items: Kitchens and bathrooms with a bright window
home_use.note: Likes humid air; keep it away from cold drafts

snap: An upright, leafy plant with glossy leaves splashed in gold and dark green, like a mosaic. It brightens a shelf or side table and is easier to keep than most calatheas. It likes soft light and humid air. Generally regarded as safe for cats and dogs.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Native to the rainforests of Brazil, where it grows on the shaded forest floor. That is why it wants warmth, humidity and soft light, not hot sun. A clumping plant with upright stems that usually reaches 60–90 cm indoors, and often looks best with a stake for support.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Give it soft, bright indirect light and humid air, and water when the top 2–3 cm of soil is dry, ideally with filtered or rainwater. Direct sun scorches the gold, and in dim light the pattern fades. Brown leaf tips mean dry air or minerals and chemicals in tap water. Keep it warm, above 15°C, and away from cold drafts.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: Each glossy leaf is splashed with gold, lime and dark green in its own way, which gives the plant its mosaic look. It is more forgiving of changing indoor conditions than most of the calathea family. Like its prayer-plant relatives, its leaves shift with the light through the day. Wipe the leaves gently with a damp cloth to keep the gloss.
